_about.purpose: Curated decisions applied on top of the original draft (data/atlas_v2.json), which is kept untouched for provenance.
_about.rule: Every correction records who decided it, why, and where the replacement came from. Gene symbols introduced here are resolved by the pipeline like any other — a correction is an instruction, never a verification.
_about.pinning_note: Where a gene family could not be pinned to a named ortholog in the stated crop, it is listed in unpinned[] rather than replaced by a guess.
_about.alias_note: search_aliases map a literature symbol to the symbol NCBI actually indexes. They widen the search; they never assert the genes are the same — the pipeline still has to find a record, and the corroboration used here is chromosome agreement with the locus ID.
_about.locus_identity_note: gene_locus ties a literature symbol to its genome locus tag. When NCBI Gene holds no record for the symbol, the pipeline resolves identity from the GenBank record that carries that locus_tag, reading /product and /protein_id off the record itself.
_about.accession_note: gene_accession pins a symbol to a specific GenBank record when neither NCBI Gene nor a locus tag resolves it. The pipeline fetches the record and reads its organism, gene name and product, so a wrong accession fails loudly instead of being trusted.
_about.id_note: gene_ncbi_id pins a symbol to an NCBI Gene record by ID. The pipeline fetches the record and checks the organism, so a wrong ID fails loudly.
_about.commercial_rule: Level 1 means THIS entry's genetic solution is in a commercial product — not that a product exists with the same trait by another route. commercial_product is set only when a source ties the named product to the entry's gene or allele.
_about.journal_note: citation_journals supply the journal a draft citation omitted. They widen the search by one well-defined step; the match still has to find a paper by that author, in that year, in that journal, whose title carries the trait. A wrong journal simply fails.
_about.max_level_note: max_level caps what the derivation may claim for an entry, with a reason. Used for network entries where a confirmed paper about the trait is not functional validation of each gene listed.
_about.locus_sources: Locus tags are resolved at Sol Genomics Network for Solanaceae, in the Ensembl Genomes plants annotation for cucurbits and Brassicas, in the eggplant V4 annotation that Sol Genomics hosts, and at GenBank where a record carries the tag. Ensembl's REST service for plants is gone (rest.ensemblgenomes.org serves a certificate for another host, plants.ensembl.org redirects to an unreachable one), so the annotation files are the stable route. cucurbitgenomics.org serves no working HTTPS.
_about.transfer_entries: An entry may document a solution in one species and target another — that is what this atlas is for. documented_in names the species the evidence comes from, gene_species tells the pipeline which organism to identify the gene in, and target_note states what is known about the target crop. Without these a transfer entry looks like a failed lookup.
_about.new_entries: Entries added after the original draft. They live here rather than in atlas_v2.json so the draft stays untouched and the difference between what a tool proposed and what a breeder added stays visible.
_about.level1_rule: Level 1 means THIS SOLUTION — the mechanism — was commercially applied, not that the trait is commercially available by some other route. Decided by the maintainer on 2026-11-16, with the reasoning that mechanism and allele are not the same thing: two programmes can target the same gene by the same method and still end up with different alleles, because CRISPR repair produces different indels each time. So unless the entry describes the product's own sequence, the honest claim is that the mechanism was deployed, never that the entry's allele is in the product. Each Level 1 entry therefore records commercial_basis: 'mechanism' where the route was reproduced, or 'allele' where the product carries the very allele the entry names, which is what introgression does.
_about.ip_rule: An IP signal needs a patent publication number — a WO, EP, US or other identifier that can be looked up. 'This area is heavily patented' is a lead, not a signal: it cannot be checked, it cannot be dated, and it cannot tell a breeder whether the specific route they want is blocked. Patent databases are not reachable from the build environment, so no entry's IP field is machine-verified; every one of them is a research signal and none is legal advice or a freedom-to-operate opinion.

EGG-PRICKLE-01.decision: Replace the draft's SmMYB candidates with SmLOG1 as the gene, keeping SmMYB recorded as a superseded candidate.
EGG-PRICKLE-01.rationale: PMID 38974191 fine-mapped the PE locus on chromosome 6 to a 9233 bp interval holding one candidate, SmLOG1, a LONELY GUY family cytokinin biosynthetic enzyme, and CRISPR-Cas9 knockout of it abolished prickles in all tissues. The draft's SmMYB candidates are a different gene and that paper does not support them.

set.gene_function: LONELY GUY (LOG) family cytokinin biosynthetic enzyme; expressed mainly in immature prickles.
set.editing_possibility: Promoter editing, or marker-assisted selection on the CAPS marker at -735 bp: the causal variation reported is non-coding, so a coding knockout is not the route the natural prickleless allele uses.
set.trait_inheritance: Single dominant nuclear gene (PE locus, chromosome 6)

superseded.why: Not supported by PMID 38974191. Kept here so the earlier hypothesis is not silently erased; if another source supports an SmMYB role, it can return as its own entry.

EGG-PRICKLE-01.second_suggestion_note: A later suggestion attributed PMID 38974191 to 'Satterlee et al., 2024, Science'. That is wrong and contradicts the same supplier's earlier, correct attribution: the paper is Zhang L, Horticulture Research 2024. It also offered the locus tag SMEL4.1_06g011220.1.01, which cannot be checked here because eggplant has no NCBI build.
EGG-PRICKLE-01.journals_from: external AI suggestion (Gemini), 2026-11-13; unverified until a match lands
EGG-PRICKLE-01.open_question: The locus resolves in the eggplant V4 annotation on chromosome 6, which is where PMID 38974191 fine-mapped the PE locus — so the position agrees. But V4 annotates it 'Protein of unknown function', so the annotation does NOT corroborate a LONELY GUY cytokinin enzyme. Identity here is positional, not functional: the paper is the only source for what the gene does.

max_level.why: Identity here is positional only. The locus exists on chromosome 6, where the paper mapped the PE locus, but the V4 annotation calls it 'Protein of unknown function', so nothing independent confirms it is a LONELY GUY cytokinin enzyme — and the symbol-to-locus assignment came from an external suggestion, not from the paper. Level 2 would claim functional validation of a gene whose identity rests on agreement of chromosome number.

GAP-COMB-01.decision: Pin the gene families to named tomato orthologs so the entry stops naming families as if they were targets. Tomato chosen as the reference crop because it is the best annotated of the three the draft listed.
GAP-COMB-01.rationale: Symbols resolved by querying NCBI Gene for Solanum lycopersicum.
unpinned: HKT1;2 — no gene of that name is annotated for Solanum lycopersicum in NCBI Gene. The draft's HKT1;2 claim most likely refers to SlHKT1;2 from the S. pennellii introgression literature, which is a different (cisgenic) route and should become its own entry rather than part of this network.
GAP-COMB-01.journals_from: external AI suggestion (Gemini), 2026-11-13; unverified until a match lands

max_level.why: Network entry: the genes were pinned to tomato orthologs, but a confirmed paper about combined drought, heat and salinity stress does not functionally validate SOS1, SOS2, NHX1, DREB2 and HsfA2 individually. Capped at Level 3 until a paper tests a named gene in a named crop.

GAP-REPRO-01.decision: Pin to named tomato orthologs; keep the unpinnable part explicit.
GAP-REPRO-01.rationale: Symbols resolved by querying NCBI Gene for Solanum lycopersicum.
unpinned: ROS scavengers — a functional class, not a gene; APX1 above is one member and stands for itself.
MADS-box regulators — too generic to pin; needs a specific gene before it can be an entry.
GAP-REPRO-01.journals_from: external AI suggestion (Gemini), 2026-11-13; unverified until a match lands

max_level.why: Network entry: same reason. A paper on pollen thermotolerance is not functional validation of HsfA2, HSP70 and APX1 one by one.

GAP-RECOV-01.decision: Pin what resolves; leave the rest as an open research question rather than an entry.
GAP-RECOV-01.rationale: Symbols resolved by querying NCBI Gene for Solanum lycopersicum.
unpinned: WOX, PLT (PLETHORA), LBD, DRO1 — none are annotated under those names for Solanum lycopersicum in NCBI Gene. Root-architecture work in tomato uses different symbols; until one is named, post-stress root recovery stays a research question, not an atlas target.

max_level.why: Network entry: same reason. Post-stress recovery frameworks do not validate CYP707A1 as a recovery target.

TOM-VITD-01.decided_by: maintainer, 2026-11-13, from an external AI suggestion (Gemini) checked against NCBI
TOM-VITD-01.decision: Keep Sl7-DR2 as the literature symbol and search NCBI under DWF5-2, the symbol it indexes.
TOM-VITD-01.rationale: The suggestion's NCBI id LOC101268773 is wrong: that record is 'protein YIP4b-like' on chromosome 7 and has nothing to do with sterols. The tomato 7-dehydrocholesterol reductase in NCBI Gene is DWF5-2 (101256596) on chromosome 6, which agrees with the claimed locus Solyc06g074090 being a chromosome-6 tag. A second 7-DHC reductase exists on chromosome 1 (LOC101248602), so the chromosome match is corroboration, not proof: confirm against the paper before calling it settled.

TOM-TOBRFV-01.decided_by: maintainer, 2026-11-13, from an external AI suggestion (Gemini) checked against NCBI
TOM-TOBRFV-01.decision: Search the TOM genes under the older GenBank symbols NCBI indexes: LeTH3/TH3 and LeTH1/TH1.
TOM-TOBRFV-01.rationale: Confirmed in NCBI: TH3 (778361, alias LeTH3) is 'tobamovirus multiplication 1 homolog 3' on chromosome 2, and TH1 (778313, alias LeTH1) is 'tobamovirus multiplication 1 homolog' on chromosome 4. Both RefSeq proteins given in the suggestion check out: NP_001234306.1 is homolog 3 and NP_001234096.1 is homolog. The chromosomes agree with the suggested loci (SlTOM1a = Solyc02g080370 on chr2, SlTOM3 = Solyc04g008540 on chr4), which means the NCBI names run opposite to the paper's: the gene the paper calls SlTOM1a is indexed as homolog 3. Anyone editing these must key on the locus tag, not the number in the symbol.
TOM-TOBRFV-01.open_question: The draft's second locus, Solyc01g105140, resolves at Sol Genomics to an RNA-binding protein, while the TOM genes resolve as tobamovirus multiplication proteins (Solyc02g080370 and Solyc04g008540, both confirmed). The draft's locus is therefore probably wrong for this entry. Gene identity itself is settled through NCBI TH3/TH1, so this is a stale identifier to remove rather than a gap in the evidence.

CUC-BITTER-01.decided_by: maintainer, 2026-11-13, from an external AI suggestion (Gemini) checked against NCBI
CUC-BITTER-01.decision: Resolve the three bitterness genes by their GenBank records rather than NCBI Gene symbols.
CUC-BITTER-01.rationale: The suggestion's NCBI ids for Bt and Bl are wrong genes: LOC101214378 is 'UPF0307 protein ECA0281' on chromosome 3 and LOC101214672 is a leucine-rich repeat extensin on chromosome 5. The loci themselves do resolve, in GenBank, with the locus tag on the record: Csa5G157230 = KM655852, bHLH transcription factor, protein AIT72027.1 (Bt); Csa5G156220 = KM655851, bHLH transcription factor, AIT72026.1 (Bl); Csa6G088690 = KM655855, oxidosqualene cyclase, AIT72030.1 (Bi). The cucurbitadienol synthase in NCBI Gene (LOC101204533, chromosome 6) agrees with Bi's chromosome.

locus_identity.Bt (Csa5G157230): GenBank KM655852, bHLH transcription factor, protein AIT72027.1
locus_identity.Bl (Csa5G156220): GenBank KM655851, bHLH transcription factor, protein AIT72026.1
locus_identity.Bi (Csa6G088690): GenBank KM655855, oxidosqualene cyclase, protein AIT72030.1

CUC-BITTER-01.commercial_status: NOT set to Level 1. 'Marketmore' and 'Spacemaster' are long-standing cucumber cultivars, and the claim that they were 'engineered or selected' for tissue-specific bitterness regulation conflates ordinary non-bitter fruit with the Bt/Bl regulatory solution described in PMID 25430763. Non-bitter fruit in cucumber predates that work by decades.

TOM-TYLCV-01.decided_by: maintainer, 2026-11-13, from an external AI suggestion (Gemini) checked against NCBI
TOM-TYLCV-01.decision: Search SlPelo under PELOTA, the symbol NCBI indexes.
TOM-TYLCV-01.rationale: Confirmed: NCBI Gene 101251671 is PELOTA, 'protein pelota homolog', chromosome 4 of Solanum lycopersicum, and NM_001279230.1 is its mRNA — both exactly as suggested. Chromosome 4 agrees with the suggested locus Solyc04g009810. One correction to the suggestion: the paper is in PLoS Genetics, not Plant Cell; first author Lapidot M, 2015, as claimed.
TOM-TYLCV-01.commercial_status: NOT set to Level 1. The cultivar names offered — 'Camaro', 'Grand Marshall', 'Jolene' — were not confirmed, and the claim mixed introgressed natural ty-5 alleles with targeted modifications, which are different routes. ty-5 resistance is widely deployed commercially; what is missing is a source naming a cultivar and its ty-5/Pelota allele.

PEP-MILDEW-01.decided_by: maintainer, 2026-11-13, from an external AI suggestion (Gemini) checked against NCBI
PEP-MILDEW-01.decision: Fix the truncated gene string and search under the symbols NCBI indexes, MLO1 and MLO2.
PEP-MILDEW-01.rationale: The draft's gene field read 'CaMLO2 (CaMLO family)', which the parser turned into a stray fragment. The paper (PLoS One 2013, first author Zheng Z, as claimed) tested CaMlo1 and CaMlo2 by VIGS. Confirmed in NCBI for Capsicum annuum: LOC107871340, 'MLO-like protein 12', alias MLO2; and LOC107848305, 'MLO-like protein 6', alias MLO1.

WAT-BRIX-01.decided_by: maintainer, 2026-11-13, from an external AI suggestion (Gemini) checked against NCBI
WAT-BRIX-01.decision: Narrow this entry to ClTST2 and move ClSWEET3 and ClLCYB out of it.
WAT-BRIX-01.rationale: PMID 29118248 (Plant Physiol 2018, first author Ren Y, 'A Tonoplast Sugar Transporter Underlies a Sugar Accumulation QTL in Watermelon') characterises ClTST2 and its upstream regulator, not ClSWEET3 or ClLCYB — so the draft bundled three genes under one paper that covers one of them. Flesh colour (ClLCYB) is a different trait from sugar accumulation and should never have shared an entry with it. Two corrections to the suggestion: the accession it gave for ClTST2, MF497324, is a Marquandomyces marquandii fungal ITS sequence, not watermelon; the real record is KY367352.1, /gene=TST2, product 'tonoplast sugar transporter 2', protein ATQ36703.1. And Citrullus lanatus does have NCBI Gene records (185 of them), though none is named TST, SWEET or LCYB, so the practical conclusion stands: identity has to come from GenBank.

superseded.why: Not characterised in PMID 29118248. ClSWEET3 needs its own entry and its own paper; ClLCYB is flesh colour, a separate trait. Removed here rather than left implying evidence they do not have.

LET-VITC-01.decided_by: maintainer, 2026-11-13, from an external AI suggestion (Gemini) checked against NCBI
LET-VITC-01.decision: Drop uORF from the gene field and pin LsGGP2 to its real NCBI record.
LET-VITC-01.rationale: uORF is a 5' UTR feature, not a gene — the suggestion was right about that. But its gene ID was wrong: 111882405 is EDR1, 'Protein kinase superfamily protein', in Lactuca sativa. The real record is LOC111907963, 'GDP-L-galactose phosphorylase 2', chromosome 7. A related gene, VTC5 (111899617), is also a GDP-L-galactose phosphorylase, so confirm against the paper which one was edited. PMID 30080209 is confirmed: Zhang H, Nat Biotechnol 2018, uORF editing for translational control.

BRA-CLUB-01.decided_by: maintainer, 2026-11-13, from an external AI suggestion (Gemini) checked against NCBI
BRA-CLUB-01.decision: Narrow the entry to CRa, anchored to GenBank AB751517.
BRA-CLUB-01.rationale: PMID 23054353 is confirmed: Ueno H, Plant Mol Biol 2012, 'Molecular characterization of the CRa gene conferring clubroot resistance', and AB751517.1 is confirmed as Brassica rapa subsp. pekinensis CRa mRNA for a putative disease resistance protein. The paper covers CRa only, so CRb, Crr1 and Crr3 do not belong in this entry. The suggestion's NCBI gene ID 103860516 is not usable: that record is 'uncharacterized LOC103860516', not the TMV-resistance-like protein described, so identity comes from the accession instead.

superseded.why: Not characterised in PMID 23054353. The PMIDs offered for them were checked and are wrong papers entirely: 23175754 is about cellulose microfibrils in collenchyma, and 24831572 is a cardiovascular medicine review. Each locus needs its own entry and a real reference.

BRA-CLUB-01.commercial_status: NOT set to Level 1. The literature does document that CR loci have been introduced into commercial F1 cultivars of Chinese cabbage, and that CRb/CRbKato is the same allele as CRa (Breeding Science 72:21040; Hatakeyama et al. 2017), and Syngenta holds a patent on monogenic dominant clubroot resistance introgressed into B. oleracea. But the specific cultivar names offered — Kilaton F1, Clapton F1, Crispus F1, Monclano F1 — could not be tied to CRa by any source found, and 'carries a major CR locus' is not the same claim as 'carries this gene'. Needs one source naming a cultivar and its locus.

ONI-TEAR-01.decided_by: maintainer, 2026-11-13, from an external AI suggestion (Gemini) checked against NCBI
ONI-TEAR-01.decision: Narrow the entry to LFS, anchored to GenBank AB089203.
ONI-TEAR-01.rationale: AB089203.1 is confirmed as Allium cepa lfs mRNA for lachrymatory factor synthase, and Allium cepa has no NCBI Gene build, so the accession is the identity anchor. PMID 18583530 silences LFS by RNAi; it does not test AcACS1 or AcACS2, so those leave this entry.

superseded.why: Not tested in PMID 18583530. Onion pungency via ACS genes is a separate trait needing its own entry and reference.

ONI-TEAR-01.commercial_status: NOT set to Level 1, and this is the clearest case of why the rule matters. Sunions is a real marketed tearless onion from BASF/Nunhems, but BASF states it is the result of more than three decades of CONVENTIONAL breeding, with pungency tracked by pyruvic acid measurement. This entry's solution is RNAi silencing of LFS (PMID 18583530). Same trait, different genetic route: the product does not validate the entry's solution, so Level 1 would be a false claim.

EGG-BROWN-01.decision: Point the three PPO genes at the eggplant V4 annotation, and drop the draft's locus.
EGG-BROWN-01.rationale: Sol Genomics hosts the eggplant V4 annotation with functional descriptions, and its V3-to-V4 table converts the V3 tags that were supplied: SMEL_008g312490/500/510 map to SMEL4_08g009050/060/070. All three are annotated 'Similar to Polyphenol oxidase B, chloroplastic' and sit adjacent on chromosome 8 between 12.139 and 12.156 Mb — the tandem PPO cluster the entry is about. The GenBank accessions supplied alongside those tags were wrong organisms entirely, so the tags turned out to be the useful part of that suggestion.
EGG-BROWN-01.open_question: Which of the three adjacent PPO genes is PPO4, PPO5 and PPO6 is NOT established here. The cluster is confirmed and all three members are polyphenol oxidases, but the symbol-to-locus assignment within it comes from the supplied V3 list, not from the paper. Read PMID 33343607 before relying on a specific one. Separately, the draft's own locus SMEL4.1_08g017350 is wrong for this entry: SMEL4_08g017350 is annotated as a U11/U12 small nuclear ribonucleoprotein, on chromosome 8 at 54.4 Mb, far from the PPO cluster.

TOM-GABA-01.decided_by: maintainer, 2026-11-13; product claim relayed from Gemini and checked on the web
TOM-GABA-01.decision: Set Level 1: the entry's own solution is the commercial product.
TOM-GABA-01.rationale: Sanatech Seed's 'Sicilian Rouge High GABA' has been sold to consumers in Japan since September 2021 and is reported as the first commercially sold CRISPR-edited food. The edit is CRISPR/Cas9 on tomato GAD disabling the C-terminal autoinhibitory/calmodulin-binding domain, which is exactly this entry's mechanism, and the fruit carries about 4-6x the GABA of unedited controls. Sources: Nature Biotechnology news (d41587-021-00026-2), Scientific American, and a Philippine regulatory product information sheet naming Sanatech Seed and the GAD target. Recorded as commercial_basis 'mechanism' rather than 'allele': the product was made by the same route on the same gene, but CRISPR repair gives a different indel each time, so claiming the entry's allele is in the fruit would overstate it.

set.commercial_product: Sicilian Rouge High GABA (Sanatech Seed, Japan, retail since Sept 2021) — the same mechanism as this entry: CRISPR/Cas9 disabling the C-terminal autoinhibitory domain of GAD. The product's own indel is not assumed to be this entry's allele.

BRA-GLUC-01.decided_by: maintainer, 2026-11-13; product claim relayed from Gemini and checked on the web
BRA-GLUC-01.decision: Set Level 1: the commercialised hybrids carry the allele this entry names.
BRA-GLUC-01.rationale: Traka et al., New Phytologist 2013 (doi 10.1111/nph.12232) reports that two high-glucoraphanin F1 hybrids were commercialised as Beneforte broccoli and that all of them carry an introgressed Brassica villosa segment containing a B. villosa Myb28 allele, with 2.5-3x the glucoraphanin of standard hybrids. The product and the entry's gene are the same thing. Note this is an introgression from a crossable wild relative, so the route is cisgenic, not a native edit. Recorded as commercial_basis 'allele', unlike the tomato entry: this is an introgression, which moves the actual B. villosa Myb28 allele into the hybrid rather than creating a new variant, so the product does carry the allele this entry names.

set.commercial_product: Beneforte broccoli (two commercialised F1 hybrids) — carry an introgressed B. villosa Myb28 allele, this entry's gene

PEP-PUNG-01.commercial_status: NOT Level 1 under the rule settled on 2026-11-16 (see _about.level1_rule). Every commercial sweet bell pepper is pun1 loss-of-function, so the allele is commercially ubiquitous — but it arrived through domestication centuries ago, not by anyone deploying this solution. The cultivars once offered as evidence ('Ace', 'Bell Boy') illustrate the allele rather than a breeding route that was taken. The entry stays at the level its functional evidence supports.

PEP-VIRUS-01.commercial_status: NOT set to Level 1: no cultivar was named, only 'commercial hybrid lines bred with pvr1/pvr2' and a list of seed companies. A category is not a product.
PEP-VIRUS-01.journals_from: external AI suggestion (Gemini), 2026-11-13; unverified until a match lands

WAT-SEED-01.decision: Restate this as what it actually is: a transfer entry. The solution is documented in grape; watermelon is the target, where it has not been tested.
WAT-SEED-01.rationale: The entry claimed ClAGL11 drives diploid seedlessness in watermelon. Nothing supports that: no gene record in Citrullus lanatus, no confirmable citation, and a locus tag from an unreachable build. What is real is the grape work — PMID 26563346 (Ocarez, Plant Cell Rep 2016) reports that suppressing the D-class MADS-box AGL11 gene triggers seedlessness in fleshy fruits — and grape AGL11 resolves in NCBI Gene as MADS5 (100232870). Retiring the entry would throw that away; an external review recommended retiring it because it read the question as whether watermelon itself was validated. A documented solution with an untested target is not a defect here, it is the point. The claim shrinks and becomes true: AGL11 suppression causes seedlessness in fleshy fruits, and nobody has tried it in watermelon.

set.trait: Seedlessness (stenospermocarpy) — documented in grape, untested in watermelon
set.target_note: Candidate ortholog identified by protein similarity: Cla97C08G144840 on chromosome 8 of the Cla97_v1 build, closest to grape AGL11 and to Arabidopsis STK and clearly separated from the C-class paralogues (see ortholog_candidate for the score profile). This is the gene to test first; orthology itself is not established, and nothing has been edited or expressed.
set.editing_possibility: Native edit candidate: suppress watermelon's own AGL11 ortholog once identified. No specific mutation is defined in this entry, because the ortholog is not identified — so a sequence-based patent search is not yet possible either. The grape evidence is for suppression of the gene, not for a transgene.
set.recommended_strategy: Genome editing, after the target ortholog is identified
set.pleiotropic_effects: Loss of AGL11 function prevents seed set, which removes the way the line itself is propagated: a seedless diploid cannot be maintained from seed. This is the practical reason commercial watermelon seedlessness runs through triploid hybrids. Any editing route here has to answer how the line is maintained — vegetative or in vitro propagation, a maintainer line, or a conditional allele — before it is a breeding plan rather than a result.

superseded.why: ClAGL11 as a watermelon gene is unsupported and is replaced by the grape source gene. The locus tag belongs to the 97103 v2 build, which is unreachable, and is dropped. ClWIP1 is a different trait and moved to its own entry, WAT-SEX-01.

WAT-SEED-01.open_question: Next steps are now concrete, in this order: confirm Cla97C08G144840 is the AGL11 ortholog with a phylogenetic tree over the conserved domains and ovule expression; then, with a real sequence in hand, a sequence-based patent search becomes possible for the first time. The IP position remains an unverified lead until someone supplies patent publication numbers — see ip_signal.

ip_signal.reported: An external analysis (Gemini, relayed by the maintainer 2026-11-16) reports that seedlessness via AGL11 / SEEDSTICK is a crowded patent area, that major vegetable seed houses hold portfolios over suppressing or editing the gene to obtain seedless fruit, that active CRISPR applications exist for diploid seedless watermelon naming ClAGL11, ClWIP1, ClARF and ClGA20ox, and that some claims reach the loss-of-function phenotype rather than one DNA sequence. It also notes EPC Rule 28(2) excludes conventionally bred plants while technical mutations remain patentable, and that this reaches Turkey through the EPC. A second round of the same analysis named a candidate locus, Cla97C07G140950, and raised a propagation point: AGL11 loss of function prevents seed set, so a seedless diploid line cannot be maintained by seed, and patents in this area may also cover the in vitro propagation and pollenizer arrangements that keep such a line alive.
ip_signal.what_was_checked: Nothing in that report could be verified here: patents.google.com, Lens and the patent offices are unreachable from the build environment, and no patent publication number was supplied. The two literature citations attached to it were checked and are real papers — PMC9433981 (Hortic Res 2022, VviAGL11 seed development) and PMID 36982733 (Int J Mol Sci 2023, 'Seedlessness Trait and Genome Editing — A Review') — but neither is a patent or FTO analysis, so neither supports the patent-density claim. The claim stands unsourced. The candidate locus does exist: Cla97C07G140950 is in the Cla97_v1 build, chromosome 7, 28,715,503-28,716,225. But the annotation gives it no name and no function, so nothing confirms it is AGL11, and its span of 722 bp is short for a MADS-box gene with the usual multi-exon structure — the neighbouring Cla97C07G140940 spans 1.9 kb. Treat it as a lead to check against the paper that proposed it, not as the watermelon ortholog. Still no patent number was supplied in either round.
ip_signal.note_on_the_query: The report also searched the patent databases for 'WAT-SEED-01' and found nothing. That is expected: WAT-SEED-01 is this atlas's own entry id, invented here, not a patent code. The absence carries no information.
before_acting: Pin down the exact target: which AGL11 homolog in Citrullus lanatus, and what kind of mutation — the watermelon ortholog is not even identified yet, so this comes first.
Search by sequence, not only keywords: run the edited region's DNA or protein through the sequence-search tools at Google Patents or Lens, since claims are written around sequences.
Check national phase in the markets that matter (Turkey, EU, US): a patent family that never entered a jurisdiction does not block it.

candidate_locus.doubt: 722 bp is short for a MADS-box gene; confirm against a primary source before use
candidate_locus.superseded_by: Cla97C08G144840, found by similarity search on 2026-11-16; see ortholog_candidate.

ortholog_candidate.how_it_was_found: scripts/find_ortholog.py aligned the grape gene and its close relatives against the whole Citrullus lanatus Cla97_v1 proteome (22,541 proteins). The paralogues were included as queries on purpose, because a best match means little if a paralogue scores almost as well.
ortholog_candidate.why_this_one: It is closest to both D-class queries and about 165 points clear of the nearest C-class paralogue, which is the discrimination that matters here. The runner-up on the D-class side, Cla97C01G024020, scores 718 against VviAGL11 but 696 against AtSHP2 — effectively tied, so it cannot be assigned. An 8.2 kb multi-exon span also fits a MADS-box gene.
ortholog_candidate.what_this_is_not: Not an established ortholog. Protein similarity with paralogue discrimination gives a ranked candidate; orthology needs a phylogenetic tree over the MADS and K-box domains, and expression in the ovule would be the biological confirmation. Until then this is the gene to test first, not the answer.
ortholog_candidate.contradicts: Both chromosome-7 identifiers previously attached to this entry. The draft's own tag Cla97C07G144940 exists in no reachable build. The locus suggested by an external analysis, Cla97C07G140950, does exist but carries no annotation, spans only 722 bp, and does not appear among the top candidates here. The best candidate is on chromosome 8.

TOM-SIZE-01.open_question: Locus Solyc07g008100 resolves at Sol Genomics only to a clone name, 'Genomic DNA chromosome 3 P1 clone MUJ8' — no gene function, and it names chromosome 3 while the tag says chromosome 7. Either the annotation is empty for this locus or the ID is wrong. SlKIX8 and SlKIX9 also fail to resolve in NCBI, so this entry currently rests on FW2.2 (Solyc02g090730, confirmed as a cell number regulator) alone.

WAT-SEX-01.why: Split out of WAT-SEED-01, which had bundled it with seedlessness. Gynoecy and sex expression are a separate breeding trait, and this gene does resolve.

entry.gene_function: WIP-type zinc finger transcription factor; carpel suppression.
entry.editing_possibility: Native edit candidate; the cucurbit WIP1/ACS pathway is the established route to gynoecious lines.
entry.conventional_breeding: Gynoecious lines exist in cucurbit breeding programmes.
entry.linkage_drag: None expected via a native edit.
entry.pleiotropic_effects: Sex expression changes flowering habit and therefore pollination management; a fully gynoecious line needs a pollenizer.
entry.environmental_interaction: Sex expression in cucurbits responds to temperature and photoperiod.

WAT-SEX-01.open_question: No functional reference yet for ClWIP1 in watermelon specifically. The gene identity is solid — Cla97C02G049440, chromosome 2, annotated Name=WIP1 in the Cla97_v1 build — but the WIP1 work this rests on was done in cucumber and melon. A watermelon paper, or an explicit note that the evidence is from a relative, is needed.
